pr_title: drivers: flash: qspi stm32 driver supporting requires_ulbpr
pr_body:
Add the support of the requires_ulbpr property when a Microchip quad-spi flash is mounted.
Set the CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y flag to access the command

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/68622
pr_comments:
Not all the quad-spi have the SPI_NOR_CMD_ULBPR command: (for example it is not listed in the Micron MT25QL512 or Macronix MX25R6435)
--> Send the qspi_write_unprotect() command during the quad-spi flash init if CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y

Tested (samples/drivers/spi_flash) on a stm32l496g_disco which has a Macronix MX25R6435 quad-NOR with  **CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=n** (no Microchip available)
Setting CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y for a non-Microchip quad-NOR will fail !
@FRASTM what is the status on using this changes in 3.7 LTS, it looks like still waiting on something for using "USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32"

@FRASTM just feedback and question on warning

Do you have an idea on what is not done correct configured or possible fix in  zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c?

I have checked out main and used it to flash for microchip sst26vf032b with sample "samples/drivers/spi_flash"
For easier reproduction warning, I have attached overlay for "stm32l476g_disco" to be placed in sample "boards"
 (Need rename to .conf and .overlay to use) 
[stm32l476g_disco_conf.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17239807/stm32l476g_disco_conf.txt)
[stm32l476g_disco_overlay.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17239808/stm32l476g_disco_overlay.txt)

my_board is derived from nucleo_l476rg 

Specific enable and using.
`CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y`
`requires-ulbpr;`

I get warning on this and not sure on how to fix it or it will be a problem.
`Warning (spi_bus_bridge): /soc/quadspi@a0001000: node name for SPI buses`

issue_context.title: "requires-ulbpr" is not implemented in stm32-qspi-nor driver
issue_context.body:
From https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/discussions/68423#discussioncomment-8379966
@erwango 
^^ @FRASTM

I also noticed that "requires-ulbpr" is not implemented in stm32-qspi-nor driver and is needed for used Microchip SST26VF064B.

[st,stm32-qspi-nor](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/build/dts/api/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.html)

That is pressent in as example https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/build/dts/api/bindings/mtd/nordic,qspi-nor.html
That looks to be implemented in ST spi driver and I haven't found in the st qspi.

I am currently need it for the Microchip SST26VF that need this feature implemented :-(
Is there a workaround to send command SPI_NOR_CMD_ULBPR (98h)?
comments:
Hi @tt0776! We appreciate you submitting your first issue for our open-source project. 🌟

Even though I'm a bot, I can assure you that the whole community is genuinely grateful for your time and effort. 🤖💙
@tt0776 Would you mind providing a more synthetic title?
I edit a new title with less detail etc. ;-)

@tt0776 Currenlty STM32 QSPI driver binding includes `jedec,jesd216.yaml` binding. See https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/94b720845d3578da9a340ab14ed8c6a7510fcd36/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st%2Cstm32-qspi-nor.yaml#L21
`requires-ulbpr` property is actually available in `dts/bindings/mtd/jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml` binding, which is a superset of `jedec,jesd216.yaml`.
As explained in the binding, this bindins provides "Common properties used by nodes describing M25P80-compatible SPI NOR
serial flash devices, regardless of which Zephyr driver is being used.".

So, ideally, by including `jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml` instead of `jedec,jesd216.yaml`, STM32 QSPI driver would then support whatever additional properties that are provided by this binding:
In `dts/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml`
```diff
+ include: ["flash-controller.yaml", "jedec,jesd216.yaml"]
- include: ["flash-controller.yaml", "jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml"]
```
The only tricky part in that operation is to be able to validate this is working as expected.

Would you be so kind to have a try to do this binding inclusion modification, define the property as needed on your board, make some tests and if working, contribute this change ?

@erwango I will try to check this out with @kk3008
Lets see if that changes, will also "solve", there was a different way Microchip SST26VF QSpi handling write expect this instruction as 1-4-4, and not 1-1-4 as normal.

I have now tested your recommendations, and changing “jedec,jesd216.yaml” to “jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml” fixed the problem that we had to implement and call the flash unprotect function in the drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c.
But the issue with the Microchip SST26VF QSpi flash chips running the SPI Quad Page Program instruction (32H) as 1-4-4, was still there.
I have updated the required patch:
```
diff --git a/drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c b/drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c
index 4090cd41bb..1e1afe2c82 100644
--- a/drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c
+++ b/drivers/flash/flash_stm32_qspi.c
@@ -174,9 +174,18 @@ static inline int qspi_prepare_quad_program(const struct device *dev,
 			dev_data->qspi_write_cmd == SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_4_4);
 
 	cmd->Instruction = dev_data->qspi_write_cmd;
+
+#if defined(CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32)
+	if (cmd->Instruction == SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4)
+	{
+		cmd->AddressMode = QSPI_ADDRESS_4_LINES;
+	}
+#else
 	cmd->AddressMode = ((cmd->Instruction == SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4)
 				? QSPI_ADDRESS_1_LINE
 				: QSPI_ADDRESS_4_LINES);
+#endif
+
 	cmd->DataMode = QSPI_DATA_4_LINES;
 	cmd->DummyCycles = 0;
 
diff --git a/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml b/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml
index 6d7bf5105e..49d615fd36 100644
--- a/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml
+++ b/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml
@@ -19,7 +19,7 @@ description: |
 
 compatible: "st,stm32-qspi-nor"
 
-include: ["flash-controller.yaml", "jedec,jesd216.yaml"]
+include: ["flash-controller.yaml", "jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml"]
 
 on-bus: qspi

```

@erwango Sorry! My mistake. This morning I tested the flash write again, and now the flash unprotect (`requires-ulbpr`) did not work.

I can now see that I had not taken the power from my setup before the test I did yesterday with `requires-ulbpr` set in the device tree, and `jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml` in the `st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml` file.

So the flash was already unprotected from my previous runs, where my original unprotect fix was included.

I have now looked into the driver implementation in Zephyr and can see that `requires-ulbpr` is only supported in `spi_nor.c`, and not in `flash_stm32_qspi.c` which I use.

What would you recommend that I do? I can add support for `requires-ulbpr` in `flash_stm32_qspi.c` and keep `jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml` in the `st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml` file, or I can go back to my originally fix in `flash_stm32_qspi.c`

Thanks for the update. Ok, my bad. I was under the assumption spi_nor.c was a sor of library which we were already calling. Which is wrong, clearly.

> What would you recommend that I do? I can add support for requires-ulbpr in flash_stm32_qspi.c and keep jedec,spi-nor-common.yaml in the st,stm32-qspi-nor.yaml file, or I can go back to my originally fix in flash_stm32_qspi.c.

First option: Rely on device tree bindings, and implement support in driver. Note that you need to include only the property you need with use of [property-allowlist](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/dts/bindings/clock/st%2Cstm32-clock-mux.yaml#L19)

@tt0776 about the addressing mode, can't you just update [writeoc](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/a454bb9abcabc8c4dbd6cd06100f78ccf19fd675/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st%2Cstm32-qspi-nor.yaml#L50) prop ?
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/a454bb9abcabc8c4dbd6cd06100f78ccf19fd675/dts/bindings/flash_controller/st%2Cstm32-qspi-nor.yaml#L50-L63

The problem is not directly related to the ST implementation of the qspi driver.

The problem is that the QSPI flash device, SST26VF032B from Microchip we use, does not follow the de facto standard for how command SQI Quad Page Program (0x32) works. It is implemented as a 1-4-4 command, see datasheet: ( https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/devicedoc/20005218e.pdf ) section  5.21 page 29, and not as a 1-1-4 as most other qspi flash devices works. 

And we cannot select PP_1_4_4 for writeoc, because command 0x38 is not supported by the Microchip device.

I hope this explains why we need the patch. But as I have said earlier, I'm very new in working with Zephyr, so I'm sure there are smarter ways to overcome the problem.

I am preparing a branch for the change you described: https://github.com/FRASTM/zephyr/tree/qspi_ulbpr
that I cannot test (no microchip quad-spi NOR flash).

--> Could the  CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32 also flag the  call to the qspi_write_unprotect() during init (flash_stm32_qspi_init)  ?

No impact seen when running on the stm32l496g_disco : 
west build -p auto -b stm32l496g_disco samples/drivers/jesd216/ -- -DCONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y

If I follow the code, the function this change is made in, is qspi_prepare_quad_program. This function is only called from one other function, flash_stm32_qspi_write, and just before qspi_prepare_quad_program is called the AddressMode has been set to QSPI_ADDRESS_1_LINE. The point in this fix, is that the Microchip qspi flash, does not follow the standard rules. As you know Instruction = SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4, stands for command is send in 1 line mode, address is send in 1 line mode and data is send in 4 lines mode. But the Microchip flash expect address to be send in 4 lines mode. Earlier in the discussion I have referred to the qspi flash datasheet. I hope this explains the code. But it's fine, if you set the AddressMode to QSPI_ADDRESS_1_LINE in the else part. There might be static analysis programs that does not allow if statements, not to have an else part.

Sorry! My suggestion to set the AddressMode to QSPI_ADDRESS_1_LINE in the else part, is of course wrong. If Instruction is different from SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4, the AddressMode shall be set accordingly. It can be SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_2, SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4 or SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_4_4.

> I am preparing a branch for the change you described: https://github.com/FRASTM/zephyr/tree/qspi_ulbpr that I cannot test (no microchip quad-spi NOR flash).
> 
> --> Could the CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32 also flag the call to the qspi_write_unprotect() during init (flash_stm32_qspi_init) ?
> 
> No impact seen when running on the stm32l496g_disco : west build -p auto -b stm32l496g_disco samples/drivers/jesd216/ -- -DCONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y

kk3008: For our sake, it's fine to flag the call to qspi_write_unprotect() during init. But I would expect that it makes sense, in general to call qspi_write_unprotect() during init, to support other qspi flash types, that also startup in protect mode. And I don't think it does any harm on the types that does not require this.

Regarding that you don't see the problem on the stm32l496g_disco, is that the Quad-spi flash on that board is a mx25R6435FM2IL0 from Macronix. And apparently that device follows the standards.

Basically the changes I have suggested, only handle the special case, where you use the Microchip device, we use, and it takes care of the problem that there is a bug in that family of chips.
You are right, that the cmd->Instruction != SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4 is never considered. But to my best knowledge, if the chip you use, follows the standards, the code will support it correct. My change only takes care of the very special case with Microchip.

> Basically the changes I have suggested, only handle the special case, where you use the Microchip device, we use, and it takes care of the problem that there is a bug in that family of chips. You are right, that the cmd->Instruction != SPI_NOR_CMD_PP_1_1_4 is never considered. But to my best knowledge, if the chip you use, follows the standards, the code will support it correct. My change only takes care of the very special case with Microchip.

Let's limit the changes to the `CONFIG_USE_MICROCHIP_QSPI_FLASH_WITH_STM32=y` condition, especially in the context of the V3.7.0
Sounds like a good idea!
